scores.notes: The left cottage has horizontal boarding and projecting stacked bay windows; the right visible facade is pale masonry and exposed timber with broad flat diamond-paned windows. The shared tree and table do not preserve the building design.

Both show the same type of enclosed, furrowed croquet lawn with card arches, clipped greenery and mature trees in daylight. A tall hedge and gate can bound a different side from the low hedges and exposed wall; no fixed shared landmark establishes a contradiction.

The right is a closer view of a greener area by the rose-lined wall, while the left opens onto the worn central lawn and hedge gate. Those views can belong to the same enclosed croquet-ground; the daylight, trees, clipped planting and card arches agree.

The left building has wooden siding and projecting bays, while the right facade has brickwork, flat diamond-paned windows and heavy ivy. Its material and window construction change beyond a different angle on the tea table.

Both show pale garden walls, clipped shrubs, tall trees and a daylight croquet lawn. The left emphasizes a deeply furrowed patch, while the right includes a greener area near the border; that local ground variation does not establish a different place.
